source.title: Toward a systems model of catatonia: Circuits, neurochemistry, immune perturbation, and biological heterogeneity
source.venue: Progress in Neuro-Psychopharmacology and Biological Psychiatry

confidence_rationale: A current (2026) synthesis that reads catatonia as 'a final common phenotype of disturbed psychomotor regulation rather than the expression of a single disease process', with hypokinetic, hyperkinetic and aberrant-volitional components and converging GABAergic / glutamatergic-NMDA / dopaminergic disturbances across cortico-striatal-thalamic, orbitofrontal, cingulate and motor-premotor networks. For ARC-086 (one phenotype, several generative routes, taxonomy indexed on axes) this is direct support at the level of the stance. For MECH-535 it is unknown: the review inventories the GABA-A, NMDA and D2 routes the chip asked about and locates none of them in the goal representation -- a clean null on the specific route -- while its 'diverse upstream liabilities destabilize shared psychomotor networks' framing is exactly the kind of multi-route structure a third route would slot into.
failure_signatures: No single biomarker or unified mechanism accounts for catatonia across contexts; neuroimaging samples over-represent schizophrenia-spectrum patients and acute-state data are scarce.

The three named dimensions (hypokinetic, hyperkinetic, aberrant-volitional) index the phenotype by MOTOR OUTPUT and VOLITION, not by representational adequacy; there is no representational axis in the field's own taxonomy.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Catatonia is transdiagnostic and internally heterogeneous, with hypokinetic, hyperkinetic and aberrant-volitional components that often overlap within an episode. The best-supported mechanistic model comes from neuroimaging implicating cortico-striatal-thalamic, cortico-cerebellar, orbitofrontal, cingulate and motor-premotor networks. Neurochemical evidence supports interacting disturbances in GABAergic inhibition, glutamatergic/NMDA excitation and dopaminergic modulation 'rather than a single-transmitter explanation'. 'Diverse upstream liabilities destabilize shared psychomotor networks, producing a recognizable but heterogeneous syndrome.'
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-086 asserts that one undertrained or degraded mechanism can yield several failure signatures and that the psychiatric failure taxonomy should be indexed on generative axes rather than on surface signs; this review is the field arriving at the same many-routes-one-phenotype structure from the clinical side. For MECH-535 the review is the current inventory of the GABA-A, NMDA/anti-NMDAR and D2 routes the chip asked about, and every one of them is placed in circuit excitability or neuromodulation of the psychomotor network -- i.e. in gating and control -- not in what the state carries. The representational route is absent from the field's own dimensional taxonomy (hypokinetic / hyperkinetic / aberrant-volitional), which is the Q2 null stated at review level.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A review that says 'many upstream liabilities converge' is compatible with a third route but is not evidence for any particular one; it cannot raise MECH-535's confidence. The dimensional taxonomy it endorses has no representational axis, so a reader could equally take it as evidence that the field has found no need for one. Published July 2026; abstract-level read only, full text not yet accessible at pull time.
mapping.source_context: Narrative systems review; human clinical neuroimaging, neurochemistry, immunology, genetics; transdiagnostic (psychiatric, neurologic, autoimmune, developmental) catatonia.

confidence_components.notes: Recent narrative review from an interventional psychiatry group, not a systematic review; scored on the abstract. Mapping fidelity is good for ARC-086's stance and poor for MECH-535's specific route. The evidence_direction_per_claim field carries that split.
